title: The Rearview
logline: Barney discovers that Ranjit has spent nine years quietly running Rearview, a matchmaking service built on everything he overhears in the back of the limo, with two hundred and twelve couples and zero divorces. Barney tries to buy it, beat it and sabotage it, while Ted, Robin and Lily secretly chase their own files, until a two a.m. break-in reveals who Ranjit's best source has been all along.
coldOpen: Kids, your Uncle Barney's Playbook had a perfect success rate. Of course, he defined success as never seeing the woman again. Then, in the fall of 2012, he found out the most successful romantic in New York had been sitting four feet in front of him for nine years.

couch.line: Luke, it's a story. You're supposed to let me reveal things.

guests.name: Colette Marchetti
guests.role: a mergers litigator who schedules her whole life, feelings included, in fifteen-minute blocks; Barney thinks she's his conquest, but she's actually Ranjit's eleven-thirty consultation, and she calls Barney 'Limo' because she never bothered to learn his name

guests.name: Dov Abernathy
guests.role: a gentle, precise pediatric dentist and Ranjit's match for Colette; hates people who clap when the plane lands with his whole body, is somehow even more punctual than she is, and has heard all about Ted Mosby

scenes.summary: Barney is sure the litigator he met at MacLaren's is meeting him at the limo. Colette gets in and asks for Ranjit: she's his eleven-thirty. In eight minutes Ranjit matches her to a dentist who also hates people who clap when the plane lands. She leaves calling Barney 'Limo'. Ranjit reveals Rearview: 212 couples, 61 weddings, zero divorces. Ted confesses he's been number forty on the waiting list since 2010. Lily learns her file has an appendix. Button: Barney has never once been done talking to Ranjit.

beats.line: It was one in the morning, and Uncle Barney was sure he'd closed the deal.
Tonight I ran The Chauffeur. I mention the limo once, and she asks where it's parked.
That's not a play. That's valet.
Her name is Colette. Litigator. And she said she'd meet me at the car.
Did she say she'd meet you at the car? Or just the car?
Marshall. Why would a woman want to meet my car without me?
Colette. Welcome to the Stinson Express. Scotch?
Ranjit, hi. Sorry I'm early. Is now still good for my eleven-thirty?
Hello! Perfect timing. Mister Barney, this will take eight minutes.
Two weeks ago, in that seat, you told your sister you hate people who clap when the plane lands.
With my whole body.
Last Tuesday, a pediatric dentist sat in the same seat and said the same thing. Also with his whole body.
Is he single?
Since March. His name is Dov. Saturday, eight o'clock, the top floor of the Pemberton.
Ranjit, you're a genius. I'm blocking out Saturday. Possibly the rest of my life.
Nice to meet you, Limo.
She called me Limo.
It suits you. Long, shiny, mostly empty.
Ranjit. Are you a matchmaker?
Hello! Yes. My company is called Rearview. Because love is closer than it appears.
Ranjit, I'm back there every night. When do you even have time to run a business?
Mostly while you are talking.
How many couples?
Two hundred and twelve. Sixty-one weddings. Zero divorces.
Zero divorces? Ranjit, in Minnesota they would carve you out of butter.
Sixty-one weddings? I've hit on bridesmaids at half of those!
I know. I drove you home from all of them. Alone.
Two hundred and twelve couples. And I've been on his waiting list since 2010.
I'm number forty.
Still number forty!
How am I still forty? It's been two years!
Nobody I match ever comes back.
Dad. You were on a waiting list to get set up by a limo driver?
Penny, it was a very exclusive limo driver.
Ranjit. Hypothetically. Do you have files on all of us?
Of course. Miss Lily, yours has an appendix.
Baby, I have an appendix!
You've always had an appendix, Lilypad.
Ranjit, take me home. I'm done talking to you.
Mister Barney, in nine years, you have never once been done talking to me.

scenes.summary: Barney's war council at GNB. His chart shows the Playbook at a hundred percent, by its own definition. Phase one, acquisition: Ranjit won't sell, and Barney has been funding Rearview for two years through a line on his limo bill marked 'Love'. Ranjit outs Robin as a Thursday client ('Different Robin'). Lily tries to bribe her way to the files and learns they're somewhere Barney never looks. Phase two, the Playbook's matchmaking play, ends with Barney. Phase three: sabotage Colette's first date. Button: Ranjit's next appointment is Barney's assistant.

beats.line: The next morning, Uncle Barney did what all great men do when they feel threatened. He made a chart.
As you can see, the Playbook remains the market leader.
beats.title: Success Rate: The Playbook vs. Rearview

beats.line: Barney, how does the Playbook define success?
She never learns my real name, and I never see her again.
And how does Ranjit define it?
They see each other every day. Forever. Like animals.
So you're both a hundred percent. At opposite things.
Phase one. Acquisition. Ranjit, come in!
Hello! I parked on the sidewalk. It is fine. I matched the officer.
Ranjit, I'm prepared to buy Rearview. One million dollars and a corner office. Not this one.
Rearview is not for sale, Mister Barney. Also, you already paid for it.
I what?
Every month I give you a bill, and you sign it without reading. Two years ago I added a line. It says, love.
How much is love?
Eleven hundred dollars a month.
Barney! You're an angel investor!
No offense, Ranjit, but matchmaking is for people who can't close. I close. Constantly.
Hello, Miss Robin! See you Thursday at four!
Different Robin.
You're a client?
I'm undercover. Posing as a woman who wants to be loved. It's a real stretch.
Ranjit. Name your price for the files. I have a credit card and no morals.
Miss Lily, my files are sacred. I keep them somewhere Mister Barney never looks.
His feelings?
Close.
Fine. Phase two. Competition. If Ranjit can match people, so can the Playbook.
The Cupid. Step five. Sit down.
beats.title: The Cupid
lines: Tragically, the perfect man has left.

beats.line: Barney, every match in that play ends with you.
Because I'm everyone's perfect match. For about six hours.
Phase three. Sabotage. Your whole brand is zero divorces. I only need to break up one couple.
Ooh. Which one?
Lily!
Colette and the dentist. Saturday night. Thirty-one floors of elevator up to the Pemberton.
Barney, sabotaging a first date is evil.
Marshall, I've sabotaged every first date I've ever been on. I'm a professional.
Good luck, Mister Barney! I must go. I have a two o'clock. It is your assistant.
Wait. I have an assistant?

scenes.summary: Barney rides up to the Pemberton with Ted as his witness. Colette greets him as 'Limo', Dov has been riding the elevator since seven, and Barney hits stop. Every sabotage fails: the fake plane-clapping story, the 'he schedules his feelings' warning (so does she, same slot), and a desperate 'Have you met me?'. Dov reveals why Ted is on a waiting list. Stuck with no plans, Colette finds out Dov cleared his whole night for her. Barney has given them their how-we-met story. Button: he'll be the whole wedding toast.

beats.line: That Saturday, Uncle Barney rode thirty-one floors to break Ranjit's perfect record. He brought me along as a witness.
Ranjit is two hundred and twelve and oh. By the thirty-first floor, he's two hundred eleven and one.
Barney, you're sabotaging a stranger's first date. In an elevator. On a Saturday.
Ted, an elevator is the perfect place to end a relationship. Nobody can storm out.
Oh. Hi, Limo.
Colette! What a coincidence. Me, here, on the night of your date, which I know nothing about.
Hi. I'm Ted Mosby, archi—
Colette? Ranjit said you'd be early, so I came earlier.
I've been in the lobby since six-thirty.
I've been riding this elevator since six.
Oh no. We've stopped. We could be stuck in here for hours.
You pressed stop. I watched you press stop.
Dov. Full disclosure. On a flight from Denver, Colette clapped when the plane landed.
That is a lie.
I know. You'd never. You have the posture of a woman who waits for the seatbelt light.
Colette, run. He schedules everything. He'll put your feelings in a calendar.
Thursdays, two to two-fifteen.
That's when I have mine!
Haaave you met... me?
Is Limo okay?
Wait. Ted Mosby? Number forty?
Ranjit talks about me?
He says you're the reason he started a waiting list.
Because I'm in such high demand?
Because he needed somewhere to put you.
I'm so sorry about this. I'm never stuck. I always have something at nine-fifteen.
I cleared my whole night. Ranjit said you've never had a night with nothing after it.
Cancel my nine-fifteen. And my ten. And all my Thursdays.
Congratulations. You just gave them their how-we-met story.
I'm going to be in their wedding toast, aren't I?
Limo, you're going to be the whole toast.

scenes.summary: Two a.m. Barney breaks into his own limo and finds Ranjit's book behind his scotch. Ted, Robin, then Lily (with Marshall, promised pancakes) all sneak in for their own files. The files are uncannily right: Ted's favorite-building habit, Robin crying at the anthem, Lily reading everyone's file, Marshall crying at strangers at the airport. Nobody ever said those things in the car. Ranjit arrives: Barney talks about them on every ride home. Flashback proves it. Barney's own file: already matched, four times. Ranjit's method: you love whoever you talk about when you think nobody is listening. Barney ups his investment in love; Ranjit already did. Ted asks who number thirty-nine is. Future Ted answers years later.

beats.line: At two in the morning, Uncle Barney broke into his own limo.
Behind my scotch. The one place I never look, because I never get past the scotch.
Ted! What are you doing here?
Nothing. Just checking where I am on the list.
Forty.
I know I'm forty!
Oh. Hey, guys. I'm working on a story.
At two in the morning?
It's very undercover.
Lilypad, you said we were going out for pancakes.
We are. Afterwards.
Ted Mosby. Number forty. Not ready. Still describes every woman by her favorite building.
In fairness, a woman's favorite building says a lot about her.
Robin Scherbatsky. Says she does not want to be matched. Cries at the anthem before every hockey game. Blames allergies.
There's a lot of pollen in a hockey arena.
Lily Aldrin. Will try to read everyone's file. Let her.
Aw. He gets me.
Marshall Eriksen. Already perfectly matched. Do not touch. Goes to the airport to cry at strangers' reunions.
They're beautiful, Barney! Somebody has to be there for them!
Wait. I've never told anyone about the anthem.
And nobody knows about the airport. I tell people I'm picking someone up.
So who told Ranjit?
Don't look at me. When I'm in this car, I'm with women. I don't talk about you guys.
Hello! It is two in the morning, and you are all in my office.
Mister Barney is lying. When the women go home, he talks about all of you. Every ride. Nine years.
Ranjit, Robin cried at the anthem again. Said it was allergies. Indoors. In February.
Ted told a girl her favorite building was derivative. On the first date. He's going to die alone.
And Marshall was at JFK again, crying at strangers. I love that big idiot.
Don't tell them I said that.
Hello! Never.
That was a different Barney.
You love this big idiot?
I was very drunk.
It was a Tuesday. He had a seltzer.
Ranjit. What does Barney's file say?
Last page, Mister Barney.
Not available for matching. Already matched. Four times.
beats.title: Barney Stinson

beats.line: Nine years in my mirror. With women, you talk about yourself. Alone, you talk about four people.
That is my whole method. You love whoever you talk about when you think nobody is listening.
Ranjit. I'd like to increase my investment in love.
Hello! I already did. Last month.
Ranjit, please. Just tell me. Who's number thirty-nine?
Confidential. But she has been waiting almost as long as you.
Kids, years later, Ranjit finally called. I told him I'd already met someone. And he said, Hello! I know. She was number thirty-nine.
